subject: DPA: data handling during transition, rollback triggers & erase procedures
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Legal Ops <legal@terracore.com>, Sohan Patel <sohan.patel@terracore.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPA: data handling during transition, rollback triggers & erase procedures

Hi Sohan / TerraCore legal team —

Thanks for the quick read-through of the DPA. We reviewed the latest redlines and put together a concise counterproposal focused on three items you flagged in the last call: (1) rollback/transition triggers, (2) backups & snapshot retention during termination, and (3) notification timing for erasure/transfer operations.

Attached is a short playbook (DPA_erase_playbook_v3.pdf) and a tracked redline (redline_dpa_20280606.docx) that maps our suggested language to your asks. Summary of key points we propose: 

- Rollback / transition triggers: we propose that customer requests to transition (migration or rollback) are treated as a standard Service Transition event unless there is a live legal hold. We accept a 30-day transition window for data transfer, with an operational grace period for snapshots (see playbook).
- Backups & snapshots: Redwood will retain encrypted backups for up to 90 days post-termination for disaster recovery, but will isolate and mark them for expedited deletion upon validated erasure requests tied to a DPA erasure command. We are willing to add an annual attestation for deletion completion upon request.
- Erase notifications: we can send an Erasure Initiation notice within 48 hours of a validated request and a completion confirmation within 10 business days for primary data and 30 days for backups unless legal hold is asserted.

Open asks for TerraCore: 
1) Confirm whether you need onshore-only deletion (we can provide onshore wipe for EU accounts but need explicit callout).
2) Do you require a shorter backup retention than 90 days?
3) If you require a synchronous SLA for deletion confirmation (e.g., 72 hours), please specify acceptable business impact tradeoffs so we can map changes to the SLA and pricing.

Kimberly / Priyom — please see in-line comments in the redline and call out any areas that require product acceptance (e.g., snapshot replication windows).

Thanks,

Nikhil Sharma
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_erase_playbook_v3.pdf (summary playbook, 6 pages)
Attachment: redline_dpa_20280606.docx (tracked changes)

From: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@terracore.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@terracore.com>, Sohan Patel <sohan.patel@terracore.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 11:04:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data handling during transition, rollback triggers & erase procedures

Thanks, Nikhil — appreciate the clear summary and the playbook. A few points from TerraCore legal after internal review: 

1) Onshore-only deletion: we do need EU-only deletion and proof of erasure for EU-resident data. The playbook language looks close but we need explicit contractual language that backups containing EU personal data will be handled following the same onshore constraints.

2) 90 days for backups: our security team prefers 30 days for backups post-termination for sensitive data sets. Is Redwood able to make an exception for EU accounts or for accounts with data classified as "sensitive"? If not feasible, we need a mechanism to request expedited purge for specific datasets within the 90-day window.

3) Erase notification SLA: 10 business days for primary data is acceptable; we cannot accept 30 days for backups without a faster escalation path. Can you add a clause that allows TerraCore to trigger an expedited purge (target 7 business days) with a verified token and approval workflow?

Also, note that our procurement team will ask for a signed attestation of deletion evidence (certificate) once the purge is complete — preferably PDF with a humidity timestamp and link to the deletion job id.

A couple of inline redlines coming from Legal Ops.

Best,
Emily Rogers
Head of Legal Ops, TerraCore

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@terracore.com>, Sohan Patel <sohan.patel@terracore.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Jun 2028 08:32:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data handling during transition, rollback triggers & erase procedures

Emily — thanks for the quick feedback. A few operational clarifications from product/ops so we can update the contract language to be precise: 

- Onshore backup purges: we can support onshore-only deletion for backups associated with EU accounts. Operationally this means the backup artifact must be tagged as EU-only at the time of snapshot creation; otherwise cross-region replication could complicate the wipe. We will add a requirement for a "region tag" on the account or snapshot to guarantee onshore-only handling.

- 30 vs 90 days: we can offer a two-tier option. For TerraCore EU accounts we will offer a default 90-day encrypted backup retention but with an optional 30-day SENSITIVE dataset profile that TerraCore can opt into. Enrolling in the 30-day profile requires a one-time configuration and an additional compliance addendum (small monthly fee).

- Expedited purge token: we can implement an expedited purge workflow that TerraCore triggers via the Console API. Requirements: (i) token request must be submitted by an authorized TerraCore admin with MFA, (ii) Redwood will initiate an expedited purge target of 7 business days for primary + backup artifacts tagged as SENSITIVE, (iii) Redwood will provide a deletion job id and a downloadable PDF certificate upon completion. We will include the audit trail (job id, timestamps, operator id) in the attestation.

Next steps proposed: 
1) If TerraCore confirms the SENSITIVE dataset profile enrollment, we'll update the redline to reflect the 30-day backup retention option and the associated addendum.
2) We'll add the expedited purge token mechanics and the attestation language to the DPA.
3) We'll include a short operational playbook appendix that defines tagging, token issuance, and evidence format.

Looping Priyom for pricing/ops impact.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Sohan Patel <sohan.patel@terracore.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@terracore.com>, Legal Ops <legal@terracore.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 14:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: DPA: data handling during transition, rollback triggers & erase procedures — acceptance in principle

Nikhil / Kimberly — thanks for the thorough responses and for proposing the expedited purge token and the SENSITIVE dataset profile. TerraCore can accept the following in principle: 

- We will enroll our EU tenant in the SENSITIVE dataset profile (please send enrollment instructions and the addendum).
- We accept the 30-day backup retention for SENSITIVE-tagged data and the 90-day default for other artifacts.
- We accept the expedited purge token workflow as described, provided the attestation PDF contains the deletion job id, timestamp, and a concise summary of affected artifact ids.

A few final asks before signature: 
1) Include explicit language that backups will be scanned and tagged for region at creation time and that Redwood will not replicate SENSITIVE snapshots out of the EU unless TerraCore explicitly requests replication for a named region.
2) Add an SLA referencing the attestation delivery timeline (attestation within 5 business days of purge completion).
3) Please confirm whether the attestation will be signed by a Redwood security officer (PDF signature) or generated programmatically.

If you can incorporate those three items into a final redline, we can move to signature on our side next week.

Best regards,
Sohan Patel
Head of Platform Security, TerraCore Ltd.
